candidates.title: [Bug]: local variable is in scope inside its own initializer (self-recursive closure crashes at runtime / INTERNAL_ERROR)
[Bug]: remote method of a client object with return type `never` is not rejected

[Bug]: int literal beyond float64 range crashes the compiler even in a valid decimal context
candidates.body:
This still reproduces on current main (1bcb85b9), and it also affects **valid** programs in a `decimal` context. An int-literal whose value is beyond float64 range but well within decimal range (decimal goes up to about 9.99E+6144) crashes the compiler instead of producing a decimal value:

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    decimal x = ; // 1 followed by 400 zeros
    io:println(x); // @output 1E+400
}
```

Actual:
```
fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: failed to parse numeric literal
 --> dec400-v.bal:4:17
```

Expected: prints `1E+400`. `decimal x = 1e400d;` already prints `1E+400`. Per spec §6.3 (numeric-literal), with expected type `decimal` an int-literal's int and float candidates are dropped and the literal denotes the decimal value, so it should never go through float64 at all. The program should compile and run, not crash and not report an out-of-range error. Literals beyond decimal range (e.g. `1` followed by 7000 zeros) crash the same way, where an out-of-range compile error is expected.

notes: Stopped after 5 confirmed candidates (~35 min). Many other spec mismatches were found but dropped as duplicates of existing issues: #1225 (double group by), #1456 (CRLF in templates), #1217 (compound assignment order), #1522 (fromBase16/64 whitespace), #1214/#1044 (shape-based type tests), #1131/#1374 (error constructor detail ImmutableClone/readonly), #1649 (bare isolated function type), #1134/#1425/#1564 (readonly record fields, spread min length, readonly filler), #1260 (field access on nilable record), #1253 (nested list store on optional member), #1050 (filler ignores defaults), #1043 (readonly class fields), #1395 (self use in init), #1650 (disallowed code points in literals). Dropped as not confirmed or intentional: a variable that becomes a grouping key in a second group by is still spread (the spec is ambiguous); unreachable panic statements rejected (#1285 was closed as not planned); narrowing carried past while/lock/match (deliberate and sound, but not listed as a deviation in subset10.md); nil stores through a wider map view delete an optional field (jBallerina-style design); collect after group by flattening (the corpus expects it). Possible follow-ups not pursued: array:removeAll can't be used as a function value (UNIMPLEMENTED diagnostic); a Go runtime index error leaks from array:map when the callback shrinks the list; int r = boom() where boom() returns never is rejected (may relate to #1785). The master spec has no group-by/collect text, so the 2024R1 spec was used for those.
